key_insight: Interpretable machine learning identified facial patterns associated with sickle cell disease (SCD), not cancer or drug discovery, with more pronounced differences in several older age groups.
clinical_relevance: These preliminary findings suggest potential digital biomarkers for supportive SCD assessment, but do not establish clinical utility or diagnostic readiness.
method: Extracted geometric and texture descriptors from standardized smartphone photographs using manually annotated facial landmarks.
Applied a linear support vector machine with recursive feature elimination and leave-one-out cross-validation.
Examined selected features across age and sex groups.
evidence_signal: Among 154 participants with confirmed SCD and 154 matched controls in Kinshasa, internal evaluation achieved an AUROC of 0.843 (95% CI: 0.798–0.887) and accuracy of 0.795 (95% CI: 0.750–0.840).
watch_item: External and longitudinal validation is needed; cross-sectional age differences do not demonstrate within-person progression.
paper_title: Quantitative Facial Phenotyping and Age-Associated Differences in Sickle Cell Disease Using Interpretable Machine Learning
